item.title: Kujukuri Surfing Guide: Beaches, Lessons & Access
item.description: Chiba’s Pacific-facing Kujukuri coast is one of the Tokyo area’s great surfing zones — a 60-kilometre run of open sand that catches consistent ocean swell from multiple directions. Towns like Ichinomiya (host to Olympic surfing in 2021), Katakai and Taito are packed with surf shops, schools and a laid-back board culture, making it an excellent place to learn or to chase clean waves close to the capital. With sandy beach breaks suited to beginners, lessons and rentals readily available, and reliable surf from spring through autumn, Kujukuri is where many Tokyoites learn to ride — and a fun, sporty addition to a Chiba coast trip.

item.title: Shonan Coast Guide: Beaches, Enoden & Access
item.description: The Shonan coast is the Tokyo area’s beloved beach playground — a sunny, laid-back stretch of sand and surf running from Kamakura past Enoshima toward Hiratsuka, all under the gaze of Mt. Fuji on clear days. This is where city-dwellers come to swim, surf, cycle and watch the sunset, riding the charming retro Enoden train as it rattles between the sea and old neighbourhoods. With beaches, Enoshima island, fresh shirasu, and an easygoing California-meets-Japan vibe, Shonan is the perfect seaside complement to historic Kamakura.

item.title: Shonan Surfing Guide: Beaches, Lessons & Access
item.description: The Shonan coast is the birthplace and beating heart of Japanese surf culture — a sunny stretch of Sagami Bay where Tokyoites have been riding waves for generations. With gentle beach breaks, a string of surf shops and schools, and Mt. Fuji on the horizon, it’s the most accessible place near the capital to learn to surf or paddle out. Beginners can take a lesson and rent a board on the same beach where locals trade waves at dawn, while the laid-back seaside towns of Kugenuma, Katase and Chigasaki keep the whole scene relaxed and welcoming.

item.title: Chiba Leisure: Tokyo Disney Resort, Surfing, Baseball & Cycling
item.description: Chiba offers an unusual spread of leisure options — from the world’s most beautiful theme park in Urayasu to the longest beach in Japan a ninety-minute drive away, and a cycling route that circles an entire peninsula. Whether you arrive chasing rides and fireworks or empty surf and coastal roads, the prefecture delivers leisure experiences that are difficult to replicate anywhere else near Tokyo. Tokyo Disney Resort — Disneyland and DisneySea Tokyo Disney Resort in Urayasu comprises two parks on Tokyo Bay: Tokyo Disneyland, which opened in 1983 as Japan’s first Western theme park, and Tokyo DisneySea, which opened in 2001 and is consistently rated among the most beautifully designed theme parks in the world.
